coverage_gaps: Public pure-plays are sparse in the deepest nuclear fuel-cycle bottlenecks; some tightest nodes may be private or embedded in megacaps.
A large share of obvious energy beneficiaries are covered by analysts, so Layer 1A must search for obscure component and service suppliers instead of only headline utilities and IPPs.
Oil and gas can be economically relevant to the theme, but the public-market linkage is less clean for hidden bottlenecks than for grid/nuclear/power equipment.
Non-US listed suppliers may be highly relevant economically but harder to express in a US-only portfolio.
Need later verification on actual analyst coverage, segment revenue purity, backlog quality, and customer concentration before promoting any node to a stronger thesis.

memory_update.text: Energy themes should be decomposed into load growth, grid bottlenecks, nuclear fuel cycle, and power-conversion equipment before selecting public equities.
Transmission hardware and transformer/power-quality suppliers are promising underfollowed discovery lanes because they sit one layer upstream of the obvious grid buildout narrative.
Nuclear fuel-cycle bottlenecks can be tighter than reactor-build narratives, but public-market expressibility is often limited by private ownership and megacap embedding.
Low analyst coverage and narrow segment exposure are essential filters for this theme because the obvious names are crowded and often too diversified.

layer1a.summary: Broad energy theme decomposed into the highest-conviction system nodes: electricity demand growth from AI/data centers and electrification; grid transmission/distribution bottlenecks; nuclear fuel and nuclear components as scarce inputs; renewable interconnection and equipment lead-time constraints; and legacy oil/gas infrastructure that still funds or supplies transition spending. For Layer 1A, the best discovery posture is to keep reference leaders in view while deliberately hunting underfollowed suppliers two steps above the obvious demand driver: transmission hardware, transformers, HVDC/reactive power, nuclear fuel cycle, and specialized EPC/service providers. Claims below are mixed: some are supported by cached evidence, while many node-level judgments are hypotheses meant to guide later verification.

supply_chain_nodes.bottleneck_hypothesis: The market may underestimate how quickly data centers and electrification can turn into multi-year procurement demand for physical electrical infrastructure.
supply_chain_nodes.market_cap_hunting_notes: Large caps dominate the obvious demand narrative; the better hunting ground is sub-$10B component and service suppliers with narrow exposure.
supply_chain_nodes.node: Electricity demand growth from AI/data centers and electrification
supply_chain_nodes.public_asset_hunting_notes: Look for suppliers exposed to utility capex, data-center electrical gear, and load-growth upgrade cycles rather than only for the large platform names that create the demand.
search_queries: AI data center power demand supplier backlog utility equipment
electrification load growth transformer switchgear supplier public company
second order beneficiaries electricity demand small cap utility gear
supply_chain_nodes.underfollowed_angle: Search for second-order beneficiaries that sell into utility distribution, power quality, or line hardware rather than hyperscalers.
supply_chain_nodes.why_it_matters: Higher load is the macro trigger that pulls through generators, grid capex, transformers, switchgear, and wiring. The most visible beneficiaries are often not the earliest or most underfollowed.

supply_chain_nodes.bottleneck_hypothesis: The scarce layer is not only line construction but also the hardware and materials installed on each tower, pole, and substation.
supply_chain_nodes.market_cap_hunting_notes: Prefer small/mid caps with product specificity and low analyst coverage; avoid diversified conglomerates unless the segment is highly pure.
supply_chain_nodes.public_asset_hunting_notes: Use backlog growth, utility approvals, and customer concentration disclosures to identify hardware suppliers with earlier demand visibility than the prime contractors.
search_queries: transmission hardware supplier public company low analyst coverage
utility grid hardware backlog order intake annual report
substation hardware supplier hidden beneficiary electrification
supply_chain_nodes.underfollowed_angle: Publicly traded niche hardware makers can sit ahead of Quanta-style contractors in the order chain.
supply_chain_nodes.why_it_matters: Transmission, substations, and distribution upgrades are necessary to move new power to load centers; these projects often have long lead times and component shortages.

supply_chain_nodes.bottleneck_hypothesis: Conversion and HALEU/fuel fabrication may be more constrained than reactor construction, and investable public exposure is sparse.
supply_chain_nodes.market_cap_hunting_notes: Centrus is the clearest smaller public name in a constrained niche; other exposure may be buried in large diversified firms.
supply_chain_nodes.node: Nuclear fuel cycle: uranium, conversion, enrichment, HALEU, fabrication
supply_chain_nodes.public_asset_hunting_notes: Anchor on public names with verifiable fuel-cycle roles and then check whether the real bottleneck is actually investable or hidden inside private entities or megacaps.
search_queries: HALEU public company bottleneck enrichment fuel fabrication
uranium conversion public company supply constraint
nuclear fuel cycle small cap public supplier
supply_chain_nodes.underfollowed_angle: A small public fuel supplier can be more interesting than a large utility or diversified industrial with only partial exposure.
supply_chain_nodes.why_it_matters: Nuclear power and SMR deployment depend on scarce fuel-cycle inputs; even where the reactor story is popular, the bottleneck can sit upstream in conversion/enrichment/fabrication.

supply_chain_nodes.bottleneck_hypothesis: Lead times, qualification cycles, and engineering constraints create a backlog-driven earnings profile for niche equipment suppliers.
supply_chain_nodes.market_cap_hunting_notes: Many attractive names are mid/small cap, regionally exposed, and undercovered despite strong structural demand.
supply_chain_nodes.node: Power conversion, transformers, switchgear, HVDC, and power quality equipment
supply_chain_nodes.public_asset_hunting_notes: Screen for dry-type transformer makers, HV equipment suppliers, and power-quality specialists with customer diversification across utility, industrial, and digital infrastructure end markets.
search_queries: dry type transformer supplier public company backlog data center
HVDC reactor supplier public company utility customers
power quality equipment supplier small cap energy transition
supply_chain_nodes.underfollowed_angle: Look for boring industrials that quietly sit at the choke point between generation and load.
supply_chain_nodes.why_it_matters: These are schedule-critical inputs for data centers, renewables, industrial electrification, and grid upgrades; shortages can delay entire projects.

supply_chain_nodes.bottleneck_hypothesis: Labor shortages and permitting delays shift value toward firms that can secure crews, manage projects, and package complex work.
supply_chain_nodes.market_cap_hunting_notes: Quanta is the benchmark, but smaller specialty service names may be more mispriced if they are tied to a narrow bottleneck.
supply_chain_nodes.node: EPC, construction, and grid services contractors
supply_chain_nodes.public_asset_hunting_notes: Use contractor backlogs as a leading indicator for hardware suppliers; then search one layer upstream for the components being ordered ahead of deployment.
search_queries: grid services contractor backlog utility transmission public company
specialty EPC energy infrastructure small cap backlog
supply_chain_nodes.underfollowed_angle: Smaller regional contractors or specialty service providers may have cleaner exposure than large diversified EPCs.
supply_chain_nodes.why_it_matters: They convert demand into installed assets, and their backlog often signals future procurement for upstream suppliers.

supply_chain_nodes.bottleneck_hypothesis: Even in transition themes, the 'old economy' customer base can be the funding engine for new capex and a stabilizer for supplier revenue.
supply_chain_nodes.market_cap_hunting_notes: Diversified industrials may conceal energy exposure; the task is to isolate the segment with direct energy linkage.
supply_chain_nodes.node: Regulated utilities and LNG/oil-gas infrastructure capex
supply_chain_nodes.public_asset_hunting_notes: Map suppliers that sell across utilities, oil & gas, industrial power, and data center infrastructure to find second-order beneficiaries.

supply_chain_nodes.underfollowed_angle: Look for cross-over suppliers whose energy-transition exposure is hidden inside legacy industrial segments.
supply_chain_nodes.why_it_matters: Utilities and oil/gas operators remain key end customers for grid equipment, power-quality gear, pumps, valves, control systems, and construction services.

theme_map.public_market_search_strategy: Start from the obvious demand drivers, then move one or two layers upstream to components, consumables, and service bottlenecks. Use a two-lane funnel: (1) reference leaders for context and price discovery, (2) underfollowed suppliers with narrow product exposure, low analyst coverage, and customer dependency that can create hidden operating leverage. Prioritize public companies with verifiable evidence in filings, contract wins, backlog, capacity expansions, and customer concentration. Treat the most crowded megacap names as context, not the main hunt.
supply_side_constraints: long qualification and utility approval cycles
skilled lineworker and EPC labor shortages
limited public pure-plays in critical subnodes
